propositions: failed LLM calls do not write usage rows because record() is called after the except block that re-raises
spend totals computed from the usage log underreport actual token consumption by omitting all failed calls
per-step cost attribution cannot account for expensive failures when step context is lost at exception time
a usage row must be written for every LLM call attempt—both successful and failed—with an explicit outcome field to distinguish delivered work from burned budget
the fix relocates failure recording into the exception path and adds an outcome marker while preserving exception semantics and preventing double-counting on retries
no double-counting across retry attempts: one row per run() call with outcome='failed' for burned attempts and outcome='ok' for delivered work
